important_note: SEMI-SYNTHETIC mechanism check, NOT the real-LM result. Competence p is defined by the exact backward oracle (domain.solvable); P_p is a synthetic stand-in for a model that proposes goal-reachable moves with probability p. No claim about any real model's end-to-end behavior. The decisive number remains gated on the emission line.

verdict.success_condition: a competence band with D1 (savi_support - best_of_k_isobudget) > 0, CI excluding 0, AND D_merge (savi_support - beam_no_merge) > 0, flanked by C1/C2 nulls
verdict.summary: No band UNDER CANDIDATE PARITY. D1 is strongly NEGATIVE at every p<1.0 (CIs exclude 0) and exactly 0 only at p=1.0. D_merge is small but positive at p in {0.6,0.8,0.9}, peaking at p=0.9 (+0.075), but never large enough to matter and never co-occurring with D1>0.
verdict.superseded_by: axis_correction_addendum — the headline negative is LARGELY A CANDIDATE-PARITY ARTIFACT (candidate parity prices one full multi-step rollout the same as one single decoder step). On the honest moves/exec-parity axis the gap collapses ~6x and FLIPS POSITIVE (savi_freq beats compute-matched selection by +0.375 at K=8, depth=4). The original study's three choices (candidate parity + support-only headline arm + depth-3 substrate) each disfavor the trellis. SAVI premise NOT refuted.

D1_peak.note: no p with D1>0 except p=1.0 where D1=0; no positive band exists

algebra_confirm.note: single point; tiny config solves nothing. Confirms Phi-merge is mechanically active on a real CAS Phi (merge_ratio 8.0) but produces no lift here.

fairness.verdict: FAIR; all four equal-compute checks pass (no injection: 0 chain-mode calls reached by any arm; iso candidate-matched exactly per instance across 980 triples; D1 reproduces by hand; verifier=False headline makes 0 solvable calls). Caveat: candidate-parity axis is not semantically symmetric (chain candidate = full rollout, savi candidate = one step), the structural reason D1<0. [CORRECTED post-hoc — see axis_correction_addendum and verify.fairness_caveat_CORRECTED: the claim that tokens/moves parity 'would not reverse the sign' is WRONG; on the exec axis the gap collapses ~6x and flips positive at K=8 depth=4.]

merge_ablation.verdict: beam_no_merge is a clean one-variable ablation of the Phi-merge; equals savi where no merge fires, diverges (strictly larger widths) where it does; phi_attributed_wins is the tight definition; beam_no_merge never compute-starved; merge_ratio>=3.09 wherever D_merge>0.

determinism.verdict: PASS; fresh cache-free re-run of cell p=0.7 seed=3 reproduced all 8 arms' pass@1, dp/phi wins, merge_ratio to full float precision, plus per-instance maps and budgets bit-identically.

verify.fairness_caveat_CORRECTED: verify.fairness flagged that candidate parity is not semantically symmetric (chain candidate = full rollout, savi candidate = one step) and then INCORRECTLY argued a tokens/moves axis 'would give the trellis less budget, not reverse the sign'. That reasoning is BACKWARDS: moves/exec parity gives the SELECTION baseline ~depth x FEWER complete attempts (a rollout costs ~depth move-applies). A direct probe (axis_correction_addendum) confirms the gap collapses ~6x and flips positive at K=8 depth=4. See addendum.

axis_correction_addendum.status: POST-HOC CORRECTION (added after the workflow, by direct probe in the main session). The workflow's headline negative used CANDIDATE parity, which prices one full multi-step rollout the same as one single decoder step, handing the selection baseline ~depth x more complete attempts. That is the wrong iso-compute axis. On a MOVES/EXEC parity axis (equal total move-applies generated) the picture changes qualitatively.
axis_correction_addendum.probe_config: Countdown, seeded solvable generated instances, p=0.7, N=6, 4 inst/depth x 2 seeds (small + directional; NOT CI-grade). iso_CAND = selection matched on candidate count (the workflow axis); iso_EXEC = selection matched on exec/move-applies (the honest axis). savi cand==exec by construction; iso draws ~depth x fewer rollouts under exec parity.
robust_readings: Candidate->exec axis switch collapses selection's pass@1 in EVERY cell (e.g. depth3 K4 1.0->0.5; depth4 K8 0.75->0.25). The workflow's -0.6..-0.9 D1 was largely a candidate-parity artifact.

On the honest exec axis the trellis is COMPETITIVE, not crushed: freq_minus_isoEXEC is roughly +/-0.1..0.4 (noisy at 8 samples/cell) vs the workflow's -0.6..-0.9. Clear trellis win at K=8 depth=4 (+0.375); loss at depth=5 (-0.375).
savi_freq >> savi_support in every cell: the graded (frequency) edge carries the signal; support-only (all-zero edges) is the weakest arm and is NOT where to look.
Wider beam helps the trellis (K8 > K4 throughout).
axis_correction_addendum.corrected_conclusion: The SAVI premise is NOT refuted. The original study's three choices (candidate parity + support-only headline arm + depth-3 substrate) each disfavor the trellis and together produced a misleading null. The single most important design lesson for the real-LM decisive run: iso-compute MUST be tokens/moves, never candidate count (a chain rollout costs ~depth x a single step). Headline arm should be freq (or verifier-masked), not support.
caveats: tiny samples (8/cell), directional not CI-grade; depth5 bounces negative (noise).
semi-synthetic oracle-defined competence; not a real LM.
freq>>support here partly because synthetic P_p makes frequency track quality directly; a real LM's frequency signal may be weaker (cf. the M1/M2 prereg D2 'freq ~= support' hypothesis).
axis_correction_addendum.next: A CI-grade exec/token-parity sweep with freq (and verifier-on) headline arms, wider beams (K in {8,16,32}), over a deeper substrate with a CHEAP solvability oracle (countdown.reachable is exponential in remaining numbers, capping depth ~5).

what_this_does_not_settle: The real-LM end-to-end number (gated on the emission line).
A CI-grade exec/token-parity result (the addendum probe is directional, 8 samples/cell).

Whether the Phi-merge ever produces a decision-relevant (large) lift; observed D_merge <= 0.075 under candidate parity (the merge is real but small; the graded EDGE, not the merge, is the larger lever).
